/content/event/name.label: Event Name
/content/event/name.helperText: Enter the full official event name exactly as it should appear on the RFP cover and running headers.

/content/event/edition.label: Edition / Year
/content/event/edition.helperText: Add the edition, anniversary, or year when it distinguishes this event from other editions.

/content/event/type.label: Event Type
/content/event/type.helperText: Choose the category that best describes the event so vendors can understand its expected scope and tone.

/content/event/theme.label: Event Theme / Tagline
/content/event/theme.helperText: Enter the official theme, tagline, or campaign line when one has been approved.

/content/event/website.label: Event Website
/content/event/website.helperText: Add the full public event website URL when vendors can use it for confirmed event or brand context.

/content/event/format.label: Event Format
/content/event/format.helperText: Choose how attendees will participate. Hybrid and Virtual selections unlock additional streaming and platform fields.

/content/event/primaryAudiences/*.label: Primary Audience
/content/event/primaryAudiences/*.helperText: Select the main audience groups so vendors can plan the right production tone, accessibility, and experience.
/content/event/primaryAudiences/*.example: C-Suite Executives and Customers / End Users

/content/event/startDate.label: Start Date
/content/event/startDate.helperText: Enter the confirmed first day of the event using the date picker.

/content/event/endDate.label: End Date
/content/event/endDate.helperText: Enter the confirmed final day of the event; it must not be earlier than the start date.

/content/event/attendeeCount.label: Total Attendance
/content/event/attendeeCount.helperText: Enter the expected total in-person attendance because it drives room sizing, equipment, labor, and pricing.

/content/event/objectives.label: Event Objectives
/content/event/objectives.helperText: Describe in two to four sentences what success looks like and the outcomes this event should produce. Leaving it blank reduces the quality of the generated narrative.
/content/event/objectives.example: Launch the partner program and schedule 30 qualified customer meetings.

/content/event/toneDirections/*.label: Tone / Brand Direction
/content/event/toneDirections/*.helperText: Choose tags that describe the desired energy, visual style, mood, and color direction so vendors understand the creative brief.

/content/event/sacredConstraints.label: Sacred Constraints
/content/event/sacredConstraints.helperText: Record any non-negotiable timing, brand, speaker, venue, or production requirement that vendors must protect.
/content/event/sacredConstraints.example: The CEO keynote must start at 9:00 AM and run exactly 22 minutes.

/content/event/organizationBackground.label: About the Organization
/content/event/organizationBackground.helperText: Give vendors a short description of the organization, its audience, and any context that affects the event experience.
/content/event/organizationBackground.example: A global software company serving enterprise operations teams in 30 countries.

/content/event/statementOfWork.label: Statement of Work
/content/event/statementOfWork.helperText: Summarize the services and deliverables vendors are expected to provide; detailed room requirements can be added in later sections.
/content/event/statementOfWork.example: Provide show production, audio, lighting, LED, playback, recording, and onsite technical labor.

/content/event/eventProfile.label: Event Profile
/content/event/eventProfile.helperText: Describe the event’s scale, program shape, attendee experience, and any history that helps vendors understand the opportunity.
/content/event/eventProfile.example: A three-day annual customer conference with one general session and six breakout rooms.

/content/event/rfpTimelineNotes.label: RFP Timeline
/content/event/rfpTimelineNotes.helperText: Add useful procurement milestones or timing notes; exact submission and selection dates are collected later in Investment & Evaluation.
/content/event/rfpTimelineNotes.example: Vendor questions close October 1; shortlisted presentations take place October 15.

/content/videoRecording/required.label: Video Recording Required
/content/videoRecording/required.helperText: Choose whether any sessions must be recorded. Selecting Yes opens the camera, recording-format, and deliverable fields; selecting No omits the recording scope from the RFP.
/content/videoRecording/required.example: Yes — Record sessions during the event

options.label: Yes — Record sessions during the event

/content/budgetPreferences/flexibility.label: Investment Flexibility
/content/budgetPreferences/flexibility.helperText: Choose how firm the investment range is so vendors know whether to hold scope, offer alternatives, or propose cost-saving value engineering.
